issues.description: Removing OTLP LoggingHandler in _shutdown_telemetry silently drops logs and may break re-init
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry() now iterates root.handlers and removes any LoggingHandler before calling force_flush(). This is a global side effect on the root logger that wasn't there before. If anything is configured to expect the OTLP handler to persist (or if shutdown can be called more than once, or in tests where multiple jobs share the same root logger), this silently strips logging. It also assumes only one LoggingHandler is the OTLP one — any unrelated OTLP LoggingHandler attached elsewhere will be removed. Consider tracking the specific handler instance added by _setup_cloud_tracer and removing only that one.

issues.description: Unconditional force_flush() risks the very deadlock the previous comment warned about
issues.detail: The prior code intentionally skipped force_flush() because 'force_flush will cause deadlock when new logs from OTLPLogExporter are emitted.' The fix relies on removing the LoggingHandler from root *before* flushing, but OTLPLogExporter may emit through other loggers/handlers (e.g. propagation, third-party loggers attached separately, or non-root LoggingHandlers). If any LoggingHandler is attached to a non-root logger or added by user code, the deadlock returns. A safer approach is a bounded force_flush with timeout, or wrapping the flush in a thread/executor with timeout protection.

issues.description: Unbounded log buffer can OOM on long-delayed session.start()
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list[LogRecord]. If session.start() is delayed or never called (which is exactly the crash scenario this PR targets), every root-logger record accumulates until _on_cleanup runs. For long-lived processes or noisy logging, this is a memory leak with no upper bound. Add a max size (e.g., 10k records or 50MB) with FIFO eviction, and ideally a TTL.

issues.description: Removing parallel test execution (-n auto) and disabling test_plugin_google_stt.py without explanation
issues.detail: The makefile change drops `-n auto` from pytest, serializing the entire unit test suite. This will significantly slow CI. test_plugin_google_stt.py is also removed from the test list with no comment. These changes are unrelated to the stated PR goal (crash log upload) and should be split out or justified — otherwise they look like accidental commits or band-aids for flaky tests.

issues.description: Race between availability_resp send and pending_assignments registration is now fixed but reverses a prior ordering
issues.detail: In worker.py, _queue_msg(availability_resp) is now sent *after* self._pending_assignments[job_req.id] = wait_assignment. This is the correct order (avoid assignment arriving before we register the future), but it's a subtle correctness fix tucked into a feature PR. It should be called out in the description and ideally tested. Verify no caller depends on wait_assignment only being populated after the server has acknowledged.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer picks the first LoggingHandler, which may not be the one just installed
issues.detail: The replay logic iterates root handlers and emits to the first LoggingHandler it finds. If another OTLP LoggingHandler was attached earlier (e.g., by user code or a prior init in the same process), buffered records will be replayed to the wrong handler. _setup_cloud_tracer should return or expose the specific handler it installed so flush targets it directly.

issues.description: _on_cleanup catches bare Exception when initializing crash log upload, masking failure modes
issues.detail: The try/except around init_recording in _on_cleanup swallows all exceptions and only logs. If RecordingOptions import fails, network setup fails, or auth fails, the crash logs that motivated this PR are silently lost. At minimum, log the failure with enough context to debug (job id, url), and consider narrowing the except clause.

issues.description: init_recording semantics changed: now stops buffering even when called with no-op path
issues.detail: Previously, `if self._recording_initialized or not is_cloud(...)` was a guard returning early. Now it also calls _stop_log_buffering() in that branch. If a user (or _on_cleanup) calls init_recording when _recording_initialized is already True, buffering is stopped *without* replay — discarding crash logs. The control flow conflates two cases (already-initialized vs not-cloud) with the same side effect. Split these cases explicitly.

issues.description: process_closed event now fires on both init-failure path and normal-close path
issues.detail: proc_pool.py emits 'process_closed' when initialization fails. Test code (test_ipc.py) was updated to handle proc.pid being None in the failure case. This is a semantic change to the event contract — listeners now need to handle a process that never started. Document this in the event signature or a docstring so external listeners aren't surprised.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler has no level filter — captures everything at root
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler doesn't set a level, so it inherits whatever level the root logger has (typically WARNING by default but DEBUG in many setups). For crash log fidelity that's fine, but combined with the unbounded buffer it amplifies memory pressure. Consider setting an explicit minimum level matching what OTLP would have captured.

issues.description: Local import inside _flush_early_log_buffer and _on_cleanup is a minor smell
issues.detail: Both `from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggingHandler` and `from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions` are imported inside method bodies. Likely to avoid circular imports, but it's worth a comment to document why so future maintainers don't 'clean up' by hoisting them to module scope.

issues.description: _ShutdownInfo set with user_initiated=False on crash — verify downstream consumers handle this
issues.detail: When _on_entry_done forces shutdown after a crash, it sets user_initiated=False, reason='job crashed'. Confirm that downstream cleanup, metrics, and reconnection logic treat this reason string the same as other non-user shutdowns. If 'job crashed' triggers different code paths elsewhere (e.g., retry policy), it should be a known enum value rather than a free-form string.

dissents.topic: Whether removing -n auto from unit tests is in-scope for this PR

positions.position: It's likely a fix for test isolation issues with the new global logging side effects (root logger handlers, buffering). Serial execution may be required for correctness given how heavily this PR mutates root logger state, in which case it belongs here.
Unrelated to crash log upload. Should be a separate PR with its own justification. Bundling silently slows CI for everyone and hides intent in the diff.

dissents.topic: Whether force_flush() should be re-enabled at all

positions.position: Re-enabling force_flush is correct: without it, buffered OTLP records are dropped on shutdown. The previous code was a known data-loss bug papered over with a comment.

The original comment was a deliberate safeguard. Removing the LoggingHandler before flush is fragile — any non-root LoggingHandler still deadlocks. A bounded timeout flush in a worker thread is safer than trusting handler enumeration.

dissents.topic: Stopping buffering inside the already-initialized branch of init_recording

positions.position: Calling _stop_log_buffering() unconditionally when init_recording returns early ensures the handler is cleaned up if init_recording is called twice. Safer to err on the side of cleanup.

Conflates two distinct early-return cases (already initialized vs not-cloud). If buffering was started and init_recording is then called a second time before replay, we silently lose crash logs. The branches should be separated.

review.summary: This PR fixes a real and important bug: crash logs before session.start() were lost, making production troubleshooting hard. The overall approach (buffer early, replay through OTLP once available, force-trigger shutdown on early crash) is sound. However, the implementation introduces several risky global side effects on the root logger and re-enables a force_flush that was previously disabled due to deadlock — the new safeguard (handler removal before flush) is fragile and depends on enumerating exactly one LoggingHandler on root. The unbounded log buffer is a latent OOM risk in exactly the crash-delay scenarios this PR targets. Unrelated changes (removing pytest -n auto, dropping a test file, worker.py message ordering fix) are bundled in and should be split or justified. Recommend addressing the P0s (bounded buffer, scoped handler removal, safer flush) before merge.
